A general procedure for the HgC1,-mediated monolithiation reaction of 1-phenyl-l-allrynes was de- 
Keywor~I~ Ha, monolithiation, 1-phenyl-l-alkynes, monobenzylation, monoallylation, 
Carbon-carbon bond formation via a reaction of an organometallic reagent with an akyl halide is one 
of the most efficient pathways in organic synthesis. I The reaction of organolithiums with organic halides is 
one of them. ‘J Usually, organolithiums can be prepared via the following reactions: ( 1) the oxidative 
addition reaction of organic halides with the metallic lithium;’(2) halogen-lithium exchange reaction of 
organic  halide^;^ ( 3) depmtonation reaction of compounds bearing activated C-H bond with BuLi, or 
IDA, etc . Recently, during ow study on the new methodology for the concise synthesis of 1 ,4-diaryl-l- 
alkynes we developed a new HgClp~italyzd monolithiation reaction of 1-aryl-l-pmpynes.’ The organo- 
lithiums formed via the reaction of l-aryl-l-pmpynes with 1 equiv. of n-BuLi reacted smoothly with ben- 
zylic halides to afford 1,4-diaryl-l-pmpynes as the major products (Q. 1) .5 In this paper, we wish to 
discuss our recent results on the monolithiation reaction of l-phenyl-l-alkynes other than l-aryl-l-pmpy- 
nes and the subsequent alkylation reaction ( including benzylation and allylation ) , as well as the mono - 
allylation reaction of l-phenyl-l-pmpyne .

The pmpargylic lithiums formed by the HgC12-catalyzed monolihation also reacted with allylic 
halides, some representative results are summarized in Table 1. The following points should be noted: 
(1) the monoallylation reaction of 1-phenyl-1-propyne afforded 1-phenyl-5-en-1-ynes as the major pd- 
ucts (Entries 1-4, Table 1); (2) the monoallylation reaction of 1-phenyl-1-butyne (lb), l-phenyl-l- 
hexyne ( Ic) , and 1 ,4-diphenyl-l-butyne (Id) afforded the corresponding allenes as the major products 
( Entries 5-9, Table 1 ) , probably due to the increase of the steric hindrance at the p'ogarylic positions; 
(3) the treatment of 1 ,.l-diphenyl-l-butyne with n-BuLi afforded the monolithiation product at 3-position 
highly chemoselectively , while the monolithiation at the benzylic 4-position7 was not observed ( Entry 9, 
Table 1 and Scheme 2) ; (4) in the absence of HgC12, the monoallylation of 1-phenyl-1-alkynes with n- 
BuLi in THF afforded the corresponding products in very low yields (Scheme 3). The similar reaction of 
I-phenyl-1,-pmpyne (la) in ether did not occur, la was recovered in 92% NMR yield.

The reactivity of pmpargylic mercurys was reported to be slugish, and their reactions with alkyl 
halides were slow and should be catalyzed by Lewis acid or hv. Thus, as a control experiment, 1- 
phenyl-1-pmpargyl mercury bmmide was synthesized according to a reported pm~edure.~ Its reaction with 
ally1 bromide was tried. No cross-coupling products 4a and 5a were detected and 1-phenyl-1-pm-1 
mercury bromide was recovered in 90% yield ( Scheme 4), indicating that the mnobenzylation and 
monoallylation of 1-phenyl-1-alkynes did not proceed via the reaction of organic halides with pmpargylic 
mercury halides, which, in principle, could be fonned via the transmetalation reaction of the pmpargylic 
lithiums with HgC12. Thus, both the solvent effect of THF and the catalytic amount of HgCl2 might stop 
the bislithiation reaction of 1-phenyl-1-alkynes. 
In summary, we have developed a general HgC12-catalyzed monolithiation reaction of l-phenyl-l- 
alkynes. The subsequent reaction with benzyl bromide and allylic halides affoded important synthetic in- 
termediates, i . e . , alkynes and allenes, in high yields. The investigation of the reaction scope and the 
exact role of Hgclz are currently under way in our laboratory.

To a solution of propargyl mercury bromide (20 mg, 0.05 mmol) in THF (5 mL) was added ally1 
bmmide (7.3 mg, 0.06 mmol) at - 78 "c . Then the reaction was allowed to warm up to room tempera- 
ture natudy . After 10 h at mom temperatm, the reaction was quenched with saturated N€&Cl. Extrac- 
tion with petroleum ether (60-W"c ) , washing with saturated NaC1, drying over Mg04, filtering, and 
removal the solvents afforded the crude product, which was analyzed by 'H NMR spectra. No cross-cou- 
pling-products 4a or 5a were detected. hpargyl mercury bmmide was recovered in 90% yield as deter- 
mined by 'H NMR spectra using CHZBrz as the internal standard.
